trip.title: Thailand: A Relaxed 12-Day Journey
trip.subtitle: Bangkok, Pattaya, Khao Lak, Phuket, Phi Phi

stays.name: Bangkok hotel (fill in name)
stays.notes: Booked for the 22nd with a note about the 04:00 arrival and luggage storage. Ask about paid early check-in on arrival.

stays.name: Khao Lak resort (fill in name)
stays.address: Nang Thong or Bang Niang beach
stays.notes: Confirm the airport-to-Khao Lak cab the day before so a driver is waiting.

stays.name: Phuket hotel (fill in name)
stays.notes: West coast bases, all quieter than Patong. Grab is much cheaper than island taxis.

days.title: Arrival and a Gentle Introduction
days.summary: Land at dawn, ease into the city, and finish with a slow river dinner.
notes: Buy a tourist SIM at arrivals. AIS, TrueMove or dtac, 300 to 600 baht for 8 to 15 days of data.
Most Bangkok hotels will hold bags from early morning even if the room is not ready.

items.title: Arrival at Suvarnabhumi Airport
items.description: Land, clear immigration and collect baggage. Queues are short at this hour. Expect to be out of the terminal by 05:15.

items.title: Airport breakfast and freshening up
items.description: Magic Food Point on Level 1 is the staff canteen: cheap, clean and open early. Miracle Lounge in arrivals has pay-per-use showers, worth it after a night flight.

images.caption: Thai food, cooked in front of you

items.title: Transfer into the city
items.description: Airport Rail Link to Phaya Thai, or a metered taxi. Traffic before 08:00 is manageable. Head to the hotel and request luggage storage.

images.caption: The Chao Phraya, the spine of the city

items.title: Wat Pho and the Reclining Buddha
items.description: Calmer than the Grand Palace and opens at 08:00. The 46-metre Reclining Buddha is arresting. The on-site massage school offers an hour-long treatment for a fraction of hotel spa prices.

items.title: Lunch at Tha Tien
items.description: The riverside pier area next to Wat Pho. Try boat noodle soup or pad kra pao.

images.caption: Phat thai from a street stall

items.title: Hotel check-in and rest
items.description: Standard check-in is 14:00. Take the afternoon completely off. A proper three-hour sleep sets up the rest of the trip.

items.title: Chao Phraya river dinner cruise
items.description: A slow, seated introduction to the city with no walking. Book a cruise departing from Asiatique or River City Pier.

images.caption: River boats run late into the evening

days.title: Temples, Canals and the Old City
days.summary: Early temples, a long midday break, then the quiet canals of Thonburi.
notes: Buy a Rabbit card for the BTS Skytrain on day one. It saves queueing and the Skytrain is the fastest way across central Bangkok.
Dress code at temples is enforced: shoulders and knees covered, shoes off inside buildings.

items.title: The Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew
items.description: Arrive at opening. By 10:00 the complex fills with tour groups. Allow two hours.

images.caption: Wat Phra Kaew inside the Grand Palace
Gilded chedis in the palace grounds

items.title: Wat Arun by river ferry
items.description: The cross-river ferry from Tha Tien costs a few baht and takes four minutes. The steep upper stairs are optional.

images.caption: Wat Arun at sunset from the river

items.title: Lunch and a long break
items.description: Return to the hotel or find an air-conditioned spot. Midday heat and humidity in August is the real challenge, not the walking. Plan to be indoors 12:30 to 16:00 on all Bangkok days.

items.title: Longtail boat through the Thonburi canals
items.description: Stilt houses and waterside temples on the western bank. A private longtail hired at Tha Tien or Chang Pier is far better than a shared tour.

items.title: Dinner in Chinatown, Yaowarat
items.description: Yaowarat Road comes alive after dark and the seafood stalls set up around 18:00. The side streets are just as good and considerably calmer.

days.title: Markets, Greenery and a Slow Day
days.summary: Chatuchak in the cool of the morning, then the green lung across the river.
notes: If the market feels like too much, swap it for Jim Thompson House and a quiet lunch. The itinerary should bend to the day's energy.

items.title: Chatuchak Weekend Market
items.description: Over 15,000 stalls, so treat it as a wander rather than a mission. Sections 2 to 4 hold handicrafts and ceramics. Arrive early, the aisles get hot and dense by 11:00.

items.title: Escape to Bang Krachao
items.description: Bangkok's green lung: a horseshoe island of mangrove and elevated walkways. Boat from Klong Toey Pier, rent bicycles at the landing. Flat, shaded and almost silent.

images.caption: Wat Bang Nam Phueng, inside the Bang Krachao loop

items.title: Lunch at Bang Nam Pheung floating market
items.description: Weekend-only, local rather than touristic. Grilled river prawns and coconut desserts are the specialities.

items.title: Return and evening at leisure
items.description: Consider a Thai massage near the hotel, then an early night. Tomorrow is a full day trip.

days.title: Pattaya Day Trip
days.summary: A private car for the whole day: carved temple, island beach, viewpoint, home by 19:00.
notes: No need to pack or check out. A single day car hire that waits at each stop is far less hassle than piecemeal transfers.

items.title: Depart Bangkok by private car
items.description: Roughly two hours on Highway 7. Hire a car with driver for the day so it waits and brings you back.

items.title: Sanctuary of Truth
items.description: An enormous, entirely wooden temple on the seafront at Naklua, still under construction after four decades. Every surface hand-carved. About ninety minutes. Hard hats provided and required.

items.title: Coral Island, Koh Larn
items.description: Speedboat or public ferry from Bali Hai Pier, around forty minutes. Head to Samae or Tien Beach, both quieter than Tawaen. Swim and take a beachfront seafood lunch.

images.caption: Clear water a short ferry ride out

items.title: Return ferry and Pattaya Viewpoint
items.description: Drive up to Pratumnak Hill for the classic curve-of-the-bay view before heading back.

items.title: Drive back to Bangkok
items.description: Roughly two hours. Aim to be back at the hotel by around 19:00.

images.caption: Back into Bangkok for the night

items.title: Dinner near the hotel
items.description: Keep the last Bangkok evening simple, since tomorrow involves a flight.

images.caption: Tom yum to finish the day

days.title: Crossing to the Andaman Coast
days.summary: A slow morning, an afternoon flight to Phuket, and a coastal drive north.
notes: Book the Bangkok to Phuket flight well in advance. Afternoon slots that suit this plan fill first.
Confirm the airport-to-Khao Lak cab the day before so a driver is waiting on arrival.

items.title: Relaxed morning and checkout
items.description: No rush. Proper breakfast, finish packing, check out. Bags can be stored if needed.

images.caption: A last morning on the river

items.title: Transfer to Suvarnabhumi Airport
items.description: Allow ninety minutes including traffic. Arriving around 12:30 gives a comfortable margin.

items.title: Afternoon flight to Phuket
items.description: Approximately eighty minutes. Thai Airways, Bangkok Airways and Thai Vietjet all operate this route frequently.

items.title: Cab from Phuket Airport to Khao Lak
items.description: Around ninety minutes north by road. Arrange in advance. The scenery improves steadily as the development thins out.

items.title: Check in and decompress
items.description: A long, quiet stretch of beach backed by rainforest and national park. No nightlife to speak of, which is precisely the point.

images.caption: The long, calm beach at Khao Lak

items.title: First Khao Lak dinner
items.description: A quiet beachfront seafood dinner at Bang Niang after the travel day.

images.caption: First dinner on the Andaman coast

days.title: Rainforest, Waterfalls and Nothing Much Else
days.summary: An early coastal trail and a waterfall swim, then a deliberately empty afternoon.
notes: The Similan Islands are closed mid-May to mid-October for marine recovery, so they are not available in late August. Phang Nga Bay tomorrow more than compensates.

items.title: Khao Lak-Lam Ru National Park
items.description: A moderate coastal trail from the visitor centre to a clifftop viewpoint over the Andaman Sea, about an hour each way at an easy pace. Go early, before the heat builds.

items.title: Ton Chong Fa Waterfall
items.description: A five-tier waterfall. The first two tiers are an easy fifteen-minute walk from the car park with deep, cool swimming pools. Flow is strong in August.

images.caption: A rainforest waterfall in southern Thailand

items.title: Lunch in Nang Thong
items.description: The main village strip has a good spread of Thai and international restaurants.

items.title: Afternoon completely free
items.description: An intentionally empty block. Spa, pool, book, sleep. Khao Lak resorts are built for exactly this.

items.title: Dinner and the Tsunami Memorial
items.description: The memorial at Bang Niang, built around Police Boat 813 which was carried two kilometres inland in 2004. Best in the soft light of early evening.

images.caption: Police Boat 813, carried inland by the 2004 tsunami

days.title: Phang Nga Bay and the Limestone Karsts
days.summary: Sea canoeing into the hongs, the single most memorable day of the trip.
notes: Choose an operator that starts before 09:00. Day-trippers arrive from Phuket mid-morning and the hongs feel entirely different when empty.

items.title: Departure for Phang Nga Bay
items.description: Roughly an hour's drive south to the pier at Ao Por or Surakul. Book a longtail or small-group tour rather than a large speedboat operation.

items.title: Sea canoeing through the hongs
items.description: Guided canoes paddle through low sea caves into collapsed interior lagoons open to the sky and ringed by vertical cliffs. Access depends on the tide, so the operator sets the timing. No physical effort needed, a guide paddles.

items.title: James Bond Island and Koh Panyee
items.description: Khao Phing Kan is brief and crowded but the karst is remarkable. Koh Panyee, a Muslim fishing village built entirely on stilts over the water, is the better stop and where lunch is usually taken.

images.caption: Ko Tapu, the James Bond island

items.title: Return to Khao Lak
items.description: Back at the resort by late afternoon.

images.caption: Back to Khao Lak by late afternoon

items.title: Dinner at leisure
items.description: Beachfront seafood at Bang Niang.

days.title: A Day of Deliberate Rest
days.summary: No transfer, no boat, no fixed plan. The reward day.
notes: Resist the urge to fill this day. The trip's relaxed character depends on having at least one day with nothing scheduled.

items.title: Nothing scheduled
items.description: Sleep late, take a long breakfast, and let the resort pool and the beach set the pace.

images.caption: A day with nothing in it

items.title: Optional Thai massage or spa
items.description: A traditional Thai or oil massage runs 300 to 600 baht for an hour at a village spa, considerably more at a resort spa.

items.title: Slow lunch in Nang Thong
items.description: Wander the main strip and pick whatever appeals. No agenda.

images.caption: A slow lunch in Nang Thong

items.title: Beach or a gentle bike ride
items.description: The coastal road behind Bang Niang is flat and quiet. Bicycles rent for around 100 baht a day from shops along the strip.

items.title: Sunset from a beachfront bar
items.description: The west-facing beach makes every evening here a good one. Low tables on the sand, a cold drink, and no need to be anywhere.

items.title: Final Khao Lak dinner
items.description: A quiet seafood dinner. Turtle Cafe and the Bang Niang beachfront grills are reliable choices.

days.title: South to Phuket
days.summary: A late transfer south, then the island's classic sunset headland.
notes: Grab is widely available in Phuket and much cheaper than the island's taxis. Download it before arriving.
August seas on the west coast can be rough. Swim only between the red and yellow flags and take red flags seriously, they are not advisory.

items.title: Transfer to Phuket
items.description: Ninety minutes by road, crossing the Sarasin Bridge onto the island.

images.caption: South past the airport to Phuket

items.title: Check in on the west coast
items.description: Kata, Karon or Kamala. All quieter than Patong while remaining central. Kata has a good beach, a walkable village and easy access south.

images.caption: Karon, on the quieter west coast

items.title: Beach afternoon
items.description: Settle in. Mind the flags: rip currents are genuine here in August.

images.caption: Freedom Beach, a boat ride away

items.title: Promthep Cape at sunset
items.description: The southernmost point of Phuket and the island's classic sunset viewpoint. Arrive by 17:30 for parking. A lighthouse and small shrine sit at the headland.

items.title: Dinner at Rawai or Nai Harn
items.description: Excellent, unpretentious seafood. Rawai's beachfront restaurants will cook fish bought fresh from the adjacent market.

images.caption: Dinner at Rawai or Nai Harn

days.title: Phi Phi Islands
days.summary: An early speedboat to Maya Bay before the crowds, then lagoons and white sand.
notes: Seas are less predictable in late August. If the operator cancels for weather, treat it as a free day and shift the attempt to tomorrow, which is deliberately flexible.

items.title: Early departure for Phi Phi
items.description: Speedboat from Rassada Pier, around fifty minutes. Book a small-group tour capped at twenty-five people rather than a large ferry excursion.

images.caption: Out to the Phi Phi islands

items.title: Maya Bay
items.description: Reopened after a multi-year closure for reef restoration, now with strict limits. Swimming inside the bay is prohibited and boats moor at the rear entrance at Loh Samah. Early arrival matters enormously.

items.title: Pileh Lagoon and Viking Cave
items.description: Pileh is an enclosed emerald lagoon between sheer cliffs, calm enough for comfortable swimming. The best snorkelling of the day is usually here or at Loh Samah Bay.

images.caption: Limestone walls around Phi Phi Leh

items.title: Lunch on Phi Phi Don
items.description: The main inhabited island. Most tours include a buffet lunch at Ton Sai.

location.name: Ton Sai Bay, Phi Phi Don

items.title: Monkey Beach and Bamboo Island
items.description: Bamboo Island has the finest white sand of the group and shallow, clear water. Access is occasionally restricted in the rainy season, so the operator may substitute.

images.caption: Shallow water all the way out

items.title: Return to Phuket
items.description: Back at Rassada Pier around 17:30.

images.caption: Longtails head back at the end of the day

items.title: Quiet dinner near the hotel
items.description: A full-day boat trip is tiring. Keep the evening simple.

images.caption: A quiet dinner near the hotel

days.title: Old Town, Viewpoints and a Flexible Day
days.summary: Shophouses and cafes in the morning, the island's big views in the afternoon.
notes: This day is deliberately light so it can absorb a rescheduled Phi Phi trip, a weather washout, or a day of doing nothing at the pool.
Buy remaining souvenirs here in the Old Town rather than at the airport, where prices are roughly triple.

items.title: Phuket Old Town
items.description: Thalang, Dibuk and Yaowarat roads are lined with restored Sino-Portuguese shophouses in faded pastels, now holding cafes, galleries and small museums. Entirely walkable and shaded. Allow two to three hours.

items.title: Coffee and a slow lunch
items.description: The Old Town has Phuket's best cafe culture. Try a bowl of Hokkien mee, the island's signature noodle dish.

items.title: Big Buddha
items.description: A 45-metre marble Buddha on Nakkerd Hill with a 360-degree view over Chalong Bay and Kata. The drive up is steep but paved. Free entry.

items.title: Karon Viewpoint
items.description: Overlooks Kata Noi, Kata and Karon in sequence. A five-minute stop, but the best coastal panorama on the island.

images.caption: Kata Noi, Kata and Karon from the viewpoint

items.title: Farewell dinner
items.description: Consider a cliffside restaurant near Kata Noi or Nai Harn for the last evening.

items.title: Pack and prepare
items.description: Confirm the airport transfer for the morning.

images.caption: One last look at the coast

days.title: Homeward
days.summary: A calm final morning and a midday flight home.
notes: From Kata or Karon allow seventy-five minutes to the airport including traffic. From Kamala, around fifty.

items.title: Breakfast and checkout
items.description: Standard checkout is 11:00 or 12:00, comfortably ahead of the transfer.

items.title: Transfer to Phuket International Airport
items.description: Departing at 08:45 gives a comfortable margin for a 12:30 flight.

images.caption: The road north to the airport

items.title: Arrive at the airport
items.description: Just over two hours before departure. Phuket airport is compact and check-in is usually quick, but shoulder-season crowds at the international terminal can be uneven.

items.title: Departure
items.description: Flight home to India.

info.title: Visa
info.body: Indian passport holders receive visa-free entry to Thailand for stays up to 60 days under the current arrangement. Verify close to departure, as this policy has been revised several times. Carry proof of onward travel and hotel bookings.

info.title: Weather in late August
info.body: The Andaman coast is in the monsoon tail. Expect clear mornings and short intense afternoon showers of an hour or two. Temperatures 26 to 32 degrees with high humidity. Pack a light rain shell rather than an umbrella, and quick-dry clothing.

info.title: Money
info.body: The Thai baht is the only accepted currency. Avoid airport exchange counters. SuperRich and Vasu in Bangkok offer the best rates. Cards are widely accepted in hotels and larger restaurants, but street food, markets and longtail boats are cash only.

info.title: Getting around
info.body: Grab works across Bangkok and Phuket and is the simplest option. In Bangkok the BTS Skytrain and MRT metro are faster than any road transport during peak hours.

info.title: SIM and connectivity
info.body: Buy a tourist SIM at Suvarnabhumi arrivals. AIS, TrueMove and dtac offer 8 to 15 day unlimited data packages for 300 to 600 baht. eSIM options are available if the phones support it.

info.title: Health
info.body: No mandatory vaccinations. Drink bottled water only. Mosquito repellent is worth carrying, particularly in Khao Lak and in the evenings. Travel insurance covering the boat excursions is strongly recommended.

info.title: Temple etiquette
info.body: Shoulders and knees covered at all temples for both men and women. Shoes removed before entering any temple building. Never point feet toward a Buddha image. Women should not touch or hand items directly to monks.

info.title: Pacing
info.body: Every day has at most one committed activity. Afternoons from roughly 13:00 to 16:00 are deliberately unstructured. Skipping anything here costs nothing.
